en.name: Lemongrass
en.summary: Fresh lemongrass keeps 7–9 days from purchase in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). It is a tough, fibrous stalk rather than a soft leaf, which is why it freezes far better than most herbs.
en.pantry: No room-temperature timeline is published for lemongrass. The stalks look sturdy enough to sit in a bowl, but they dry out from the cut end and the outer layers go papery within a few days, taking the aroma with them. If you want them out of the fridge for a day or two, stand the trimmed ends in a little water like a bunch of flowers. Otherwise, wrap them and refrigerate them.
en.fridge: 7–9 days from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Wrap the stalks loosely in kitchen paper inside a bag in the crisper — the paper takes up the moisture the stalks give off, which otherwise pools and rots the cut ends. Do not trim or bruise them until you cook, because the lemony oils sit in the tender lower part of the stalk and start escaping the moment it is crushed. Discard the dry outer layers as you use them.
en.freezer: 6 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F), and this is the sensible way to keep lemongrass if you cook with it occasionally. Trim the stalks to the useful lower section, bag them flat with the air pressed out, and take out a stalk at a time. Frozen lemongrass is easier to slice thinly than fresh, since the fibres firm up, and it goes straight into a curry paste or a broth from frozen. You can also freeze it already bruised or blitzed, in portions.
en.thawing: Use it straight from frozen — slice or bruise the stalk while it is still cold. Thawed lemongrass goes limp and loses some of its oil to the bag.
spoilage: Stalks that have dried out to papery, hollow husks.
Mould at the base where moisture collected.
No lemon smell at all when you scrape or bruise the stalk.
tips: Buy firm, heavy stalks with a pale, plump base; a light, dry one has nothing in it.
Do not bruise them until you cook — that is when the oils escape.
Freeze whole stalks flat and slice them from frozen.
Keep the tough tops for stock or tea rather than throwing them away.

faq.a: 7–9 days from purchase in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and it works better than for most herbs. Freeze whole stalks flat and slice them straight from frozen.

faq.q: Can lemongrass be kept at room temperature?
faq.a: No timeline is published for it. The stalks dry out from the cut ends within days, so wrap them and refrigerate, or stand them in water for a day or two.

zh.name: 檸檬香茅
zh.summary: 新鮮檸檬香茅自購買日起，放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 7～9 天，−18 °C 冷凍可放 6 個月。它是堅韌多纖維的莖稈而不是柔軟的葉片，這就是為什麼它比多數香草都更耐凍。
zh.pantry: 檸檬香茅沒有公布的室溫期限。莖稈看起來結實得可以就這樣放在碗裡，但它會從切口開始失水，外層幾天內就變得像紙，香氣也跟著走。如果只想在冰箱外放個一兩天，請把修剪過的末端插進一點水裡，像插花一樣。否則，請包好冷藏。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下，自購買日起 7～9 天。請用廚房紙巾把莖稈鬆鬆包起來、裝袋放蔬果室——紙巾會吸掉莖稈散出的水氣，否則那些水會積起來、從切口把它爛掉。下鍋前不要修剪或拍打它，因為帶檸檬香的精油就集中在莖稈下段柔嫩的部分，一拍碎就開始跑。乾掉的外層要用時再剝掉即可。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下，自購買日起 6 個月；偶爾才用到香茅的人，這就是合理的保存方式。把莖稈修到好用的下段，壓出空氣平放裝袋，要用時一次拿一根。冷凍過的香茅比新鮮的更好切薄片，因為纖維變硬了；而且可以直接從冷凍丟進咖哩醬或高湯裡。也可以先拍碎或打成泥再分裝冷凍。
zh.thawing: 直接從冷凍使用——趁還冰的時候切片或拍碎。解凍後的香茅會軟塌，也會把一部分精油留在袋子裡。
spoilage: 莖稈乾成像紙一樣中空的殼。
刮開或拍碎後完全聞不到檸檬香。
tips: 挑結實、有重量、底部飽滿淡色的；輕又乾的那種裡面什麼都沒有。
下鍋前不要拍——一拍精油就開始跑。
整根平放冷凍，要用時直接從冷凍切。
上段太硬的部分留下來煮高湯或泡茶，不要丟。

faq.a: 自購買日起，4 °C 以下冷藏 7～9 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 6 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下 6 個月，而且效果比多數香草好。整根平放冷凍，要用時直接從冷凍切。

faq.q: 檸檬香茅可以放常溫嗎？
faq.a: 它沒有公布常溫的期限。莖稈幾天內就會從切口乾掉，所以請包好冷藏，或插水放個一兩天。
